note: Sample-level sweep. Closed-form signal model: every sample is +-amplitude (alternating sign), so a frame's power is exactly the sample-weighted mean of amplitude squared and its level is 10*log10 of that. A burst REPLACES the background; a whole frame inside a +L dB burst is exactly floor + L dB. Frame length 2400 samples at 48 kHz, 2 s window (40 frames), session floor -60 dBFS (background amplitude 0.001), burst start = 24000 + offset samples, 40 offsets 0, 60, ... 2340 (every 1.25 ms across one frame).

asserted_hard_ends.derivation: A burst of at most 100 ms touches at most 3 of the 50 ms frames (ceil(100/50) + 1 = 3), so it has at most 3 candidate frames < 4: never accepted at any phase.
A burst of at most 100 ms touches at most 3 of the 50 ms frames (ceil(100/50) + 1 = 3), so it has at most 3 candidate frames < 4: never accepted at any phase.

At +20 dB a 200 ms burst has 3 whole frames (rel exactly +20, the first opens the segment) plus two partial frames of fractions f and 1 - f. If the leading partial has f >= 0.0909 (1 + 99f >= 10) it opens and is a candidate: 4 candidates in a run of 4. Otherwise the trailing partial has 1 - f > 0.909 and (1 + 99(1 - f) >= 3.98) is a continuation candidate: 3 whole + 1 = 4 candidates in a run of 4. Always accepted.

A 250 ms burst contains at least 4 whole 50 ms frames at any phase (250 = 5 frame widths, at most one partial frame at each end), each rel +level >= +10: the first opens the segment, so >= 4 consecutive candidates: always accepted.

A 250 ms burst contains at least 4 whole 50 ms frames at any phase (250 = 5 frame widths, at most one partial frame at each end), each rel +level >= +10: the first opens the segment, so >= 4 consecutive candidates: always accepted.

hand_derived_rates.derivation: At +10 dB the leading partial frame (rel < +10 unless whole) cannot open the segment, so the candidates are the 2 whole frames plus at most the trailing partial: at most 3 < 4 at every phase (a frame-aligned burst has exactly 3 whole frames).

At +20 dB: offsets k = 0 and 1 (0 and 60 samples) leave the trailing partial below +6 dB (f = 0.025: 1 + 99f = 3.5 < 3.98), giving 3 candidates; offsets k = 37..39 (2220, 2280, 2340 samples) leave the leading partial below the +10 dB open level (f <= 0.075: 1 + 99f < 10), giving 3 candidates; the other 35 offsets give 4 candidates in a run of 4.

At +10 dB the leading partial can never open the segment, so a 200 ms burst is accepted only if the trailing partial (fraction off/2400) is a +6 dB continuation: 1 + 9f >= 3.98 needs f >= 0.3312, i.e. offset >= 795 samples. Offset 0 is frame aligned (4 whole frames). Rejected offsets: 60..780 (13 offsets); accepted 1 + 26 = 27 of 40. THIS CONTRADICTS 'a 200 ms burst is always accepted' at +10 dB.
See the asserted derivation: always accepted at +20 dB.

recorded_rates_note: Rates between the hard ends are RECORDED, not asserted as requirements (A1-01). The TypeScript test checks that the shipped implementation reproduces the recorded accepted offsets exactly (implementation agreement with the oracle).

known_deviation_from_amendment.amendment: AMENDMENTS-REV2 A1-01: 'bursts <= 100 ms never produce an accepted segment; >= 200 ms always do'.
known_deviation_from_amendment.finding: With the A1-03 open threshold of +10 dB the 'always' end only holds from +20 dB (200 ms) or from 250 ms (any level >= +10 dB). A 200 ms burst at +10 dB is accepted at 27 of 40 phases (it is rejected when the leading partial frame, which cannot open the segment, takes most of the burst).
